steps.title: Key Context
steps.body: The Elizabethan era was a great age of exploration. Improvements in navigation, shipbuilding, and cartography made long ocean voyages possible. English explorers were driven by a combination of economic ambition, national rivalry with Spain, religious zeal, and sheer curiosity. Their voyages laid the foundations for what would become the British Empire.

steps.title: Why Exploration Was Possible in the 16th Century
steps.body: Key technological advances made long ocean voyages feasible: Caravel and galleon ships: New ship designs combined square sails (for speed before the wind) with triangular lateen sails (for manoeuvring into the wind) Compass and astrolabe: The magnetic compass allowed sailors to determine direction; the astrolabe and later the sextant allowed them to calculate latitude from the stars Improved maps and charts: Gerardus Mercator's map projection (1569) allowed navigators to plot straight-line courses on flat maps Quadrant and cross-staff: Instruments for measuring the angle of the sun or stars above the horizon to determine latitude Log and line: Used to measure a ship's speed through the water

steps.title: Significance of Drake's Circumnavigation
steps.body: It was only the second circumnavigation in history (after Magellan's expedition, 1519-22). It demonstrated that English sailors could match Spanish and Portuguese achievements. It brought enormous wealth to England and personally enriched the Queen. It humiliated Spain by showing that the Pacific was not a "Spanish lake." It established Drake as a national hero. It laid the foundation for England's later naval dominance and colonial ambitions.

steps.title: Why the Roanoke Colony Failed
steps.body: (1) Poor planning and insufficient supplies; (2) The war with Spain diverted ships and resources; (3) Hostile relations with some Native American tribes; (4) The location was unsuitable - Roanoke Island was swampy and difficult to defend; (5) The settlers lacked the skills and experience needed for survival in a new land; (6) Raleigh's absence - he never visited Virginia himself and could not provide direct leadership.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use specific dates: Drake's circumnavigation 1577-80 , first Roanoke expedition 1584 , Lost Colony 1587 Know the difference between Drake's raiding voyage and Raleigh's colonisation attempts For "reasons for exploration" questions, discuss multiple factors, not just one Remember to discuss the impact on indigenous peoples - it's increasingly important in exams The "Lost Colony" mystery is a great example to use in questions about the challenges of colonisation Link exploration to the wider context: rivalry with Spain, the Armada, mercantilism For evaluation questions, explain how multiple factors worked together
